name: BLIP-2: Bootstrapping Language-Image Pre-training with Frozen Image Encoders and Large Language Models
problem: End-to-end vision-language pretraining was prohibitively expensive because both towers had to be trained jointly.
mechanism: Freezes a pretrained image encoder AND a frozen LLM, and bridges them with a lightweight QUERYING TRANSFORMER (Q-Former). Two stages: stage 1 bootstraps vision-language representation learning from the frozen image encoder (image-text contrastive, image-text matching, image-grounded text generation); stage 2 bootstraps vision-to-language generation from the frozen LM. Only the Q-Former is trained.
speedup_reported: Outperforms Flamingo-80B by 8.7% on zero-shot VQAv2 while using 54x fewer trainable parameters. This is a TRAINING-efficiency claim (fewer trainable parameters), not an inference throughput measurement.
notes:
Venue ICML 2023, confirmed at proceedings.mlr.press v202/li23q. INFERENCE-ENABLING CONTRIBUTION: Q-Former is a learned bottleneck that emits 32 visual query tokens by default, regardless of image resolution. In a serving system the vision tower cost then splits cleanly into (a) one encoder pass at full resolution and (b) a tiny 32-token LM prefill. This is the production-friendly form of vision-token reduction - you reduce the LM's contribution to prefill to a constant and the cost floor becomes the encoder itself.
